newsitem.title: UK: UK should adjust tax on small hi-tech firms - BOE.
newsitem.headline: UK should adjust tax on small hi-tech firms - BOE.

text.p: The Bank of England on Monday recommended adjusting Britain's capital taxation policies to encourage entrepreneurship and investment in technology-based small firms.
The call was one of 18 recommendations made in a Bank report, "The financing of technology-based small firms", on the money-raising problems facing such firms.

It said the operation of Venture Capital Trusts (VCTs) and the Enterprise Investment Scheme (EIS), both of which offer up-front tax relief on investments and relief from capital taxation, should be reviewed on a regular basis.
"There may also be other adjustments to capital taxation that would encourage entrepreneurship and investment in technology-based small firms," the Bank said.
The report found that compared with the U.S., a smaller proportion of technology-based industrial development in the UK comes from small firms.

"While the UK venture capital industry is by far the most developed in Europe, only 23 percent of total investments are made in technology-based firms. In the U.S., 65 percent of all venture capital goes to the technology sector," it said.
Among other things, the Bank recommended establishing a UK corporate venturing group to promote collaboration between large and small firms to facilitate financing.

It also suggested exploring the potential for developing informal venture capital and creating a clearing house for proposals that have not yet succeeded in getting finance through the start-up capital sector.
The Bank said it planned to hold a conference early next year, with the Royal Society and the CBI, to take the debate on financing technology-based small firms forward.
